coinbase.name: Coinbase
coinbase.key_insight: Coinbase occupies a unique position in behavioral design: it's simultaneously the most 'responsible' major crypto exchange (compliant, publicly traded, institutionally backed) and a platform whose core business benefits from the most volatile, speculative asset class in modern finance. The product design reflects this tension. Coinbase Earn pays users in crypto to complete educational modules — genuinely teaching blockchain fundamentals, but also creating an endowment effect (once you own some ETH, you're more likely to buy more). The simplified buy/sell interface removes friction that traditional finance considers protective. The portfolio tracker with real-time gains/losses creates a checking habit identical to Robinhood's. The price alerts are external triggers optimized for volatility spikes — exactly when behavioral economics predicts the worst decision-making. Coinbase's 'trusted, simple, compliant' brand positioning is genuine, but the product design still exploits the same FOMO, loss aversion, and variable reward dynamics that drive all speculative trading behavior.

snapchat.name: Snapchat
snapchat.key_insight: Snapchat's most powerful behavioral innovation isn't the disappearing message — it's the Streak. Snapstreaks (consecutive days of mutual messaging between two users) transformed an ephemeral messaging app into a daily obligation engine. A 365-day streak with a best friend isn't just a number — it's a quantified relationship artifact that feels emotionally devastating to lose. The streak mechanic exploits loss aversion at a personal level: you're not losing points or status — you're 'losing' proof of a friendship. This makes Snapchat's daily retention mechanism more powerful than any notification-based engagement system because the motivator is social guilt rather than curiosity or FOMO. Teens report feeling genuine anxiety about breaking streaks, maintaining them even during illness or vacation by sharing their passwords. Snapchat's disappearing messages further reinforce daily use: there's no archive to browse, no content to revisit, so the only way to stay connected is to keep sending. The combination of ephemeral content (nothing persists) and permanent metrics (streaks count up forever) is a brilliant behavioral design contradiction that maximizes daily engagement.
snapchat.top_technique: Snapstreaks as Loss Aversion Commitment Device
